papers.title: Pathogens of Zoonotic Viral Infections, Circulating in Populations of Small Mammals: an Overview of the Current State
papers.abstract: Small mammals (rodents, insectivores, and bats) are the main reservoirs for a wide range of zoonotic viruses. These include the agents of vector-borne infections transmitted via bites of blood-sucking arthropods (ixodid ticks, mosquitoes, sand flies) and non-vector-borne infections (orthohantaviruses and others). Natural foci of viral infections, the reservoir of which are small mammals, are of primary epidemiological significance in the Russian Federation: hundreds of cases are recorded annually, many of which are severe. The aim of this review was to summarize current data on the circulation of viral zoonotic pathogens in small mammal populations in natural foci in the Russian Federation and worldwide, as well as to identify key issues in epizootiological surveillance and the study of reservoir relationships between hosts, pathogens, and vectors. It has been shown that among the zoonotic viruses circulating with the participation of rodents and insectivores, along with the most significant and widespread, returning (re-emerging) pathogens that pose a serious global and regional threat are also of great epidemiological importance. These are representatives of the Flaviviridae family (tick-borne encephalitis virus, Omsk hemorrhagic fever virus, Kyasanur forest disease virus), Bunyaviridae (orthohantaviruses, Crimean-Congo hemorrhagic fever virus, and others), and Coronaviridae families. It was noted that small mammals acted not only as reservoir hosts for viruses but also as feeders, ensuring the maintenance of populations of vectors (ixodid and argasid ticks, mosquitoes and midges), thereby creating stable parasitic systems. The issue of zoonotic viruses circulating among small mammals remains urgent for both the Russian Federation and the global community. Analysis of global trends indicates that infectious diseases of animals are expanding their range, thereat many of them with zoonotic potential. The key drivers of this process are climate change, expansion of international trade and transformation of ecosystems, requiring improved epidemiological monitoring and an interdisciplinary approach to risk assessment.

papers.full_text: 26 Проблемы особо опасных инфекций. 2026; 3 ОБЗОРЫ DOI: 10.21055/0370-1069-2026-3-26-35 УДК 616.993:578.27 П.В. Гришина1,2, С.А. Бриллиант1, Е.В. Кузнецова1, В.А. Мищенко1,3, М.Ю. Быкова1, И.В. Вялых1 Возбудители зоонозных вирусных инфекций, циркулирующие в популяциях мелких млекопитающих: обзор современного состояния 1Федеральный научно-исследовательский институт вирусных инфекций «Виром», Екатеринбург, Российская Федерация; 2Уральский федеральный аграрный научно-исследовательский центр Уральского отделения Российской академии наук, Екатеринбург, Российская Федерация; 3Институт экологии растений и животных Уральского отделения Российской академии наук, Екатеринбург, Российская Федерация Мелкие млекопитающие (грызуны, насекомоядные, рукокрылые) являются основными резервуарами широко­ го спектра зоонозных вирусов, включая как возбудителей трансмиссивных инфекций, передающихся через укусы кровососущих членистоногих (иксодовые клещи, комары, москиты), так и другими путями передачи (ортоханта­ вирусы и др.). На территории Российской Федерации природные очаги вирусных инфекций, резервуаром которых являются мелкие млекопитающие, имеют значительное эпидемиологическое значение – ежегодно регистрируют­ ся сотни случаев заболеваний, многие из которых протекают в тяжелой форме. Целью обзора являлось обобще­ ние современных данных о циркуляции вирусных зоонозных патогенов в популяциях мелких млекопитающих в природных очагах РФ и мира, а также выявление ключевых проблем эпизоотологического надзора и изуче­ ние резервуарных взаимоотношений между хозяевами, возбудителями и переносчиками. Показано, что среди зоонозных вирусов, циркулирующих с участием грызунов и насекомоядных, наряду с наиболее значимыми и широко распространенными, важное эпидемиологическое значение имеют и возвращающиеся (re-emerging) пато­ гены, представляющие серьезную глобальную и региональную угрозу. Это представители семейств Flaviviridae (вирус клещевого энцефалита, вирус омской геморрагической лихорадки, вирус Киасанурской лесной болезни), Bunyaviridae (ортохантавирусы, вирус Крымской-Конго геморрагической лихорадки и др.), Coronaviridae и про­ чих. Отмечено, что мелкие млекопитающие выступают не только в качестве резервуарных хозяев для вирусов, но и как прокормители, обеспечивающие поддержание и рост популяций переносчиков (иксодовых и аргасовых кле­ щей, комаров, москитов), что создает устойчивые паразитарные системы. Проблема зоонозных вирусов, цирку­ лирующих среди мелких млекопитающих, остается остроактуальной как для РФ, так и для мирового сообщества. Анализ глобальных тенденций показывает, что инфекционные болезни животных расширяют свой ареал, причем многие из них обладают зооантропонозным потенциалом. Ключевыми драйверами этого процесса выступают изменение климата, расширение международной торговли и трансформация экосистем, что требует совершен­ ствования эпидемиологического мониторинга и междисциплинарного подхода к оценке рисков. Ключевые слова: мелкие млекопитающие, зоонозы, трансмиссивные инфекции, природные очаги, Bunyaviridae, Flaviviridae, Coronaviridae. Возбудители зоонозных вирусных инфекций, циркулирующие в популяциях мелких млекопитающих: обзор современного состояния. Проблемы особо опасных инфекций. 2026; 3:26–35. Vyalykh1 Pathogens of Zoonotic Viral Infections, Circulating in Populations of Small Mammals: an Overview of the Current State 1Federal Research Institute of Viral Infections “Virom”, Yekaterinburg, Russian Federation; 2Ural Federal Agrarian Research Center of the Ural Branch of the Russian Academy of Sciences, Yekaterinburg, Russian Federation; 3Institute of Plant and Animal Ecology of the Ural Branch of the Russian Academy of Sciences, Ekaterinburg, Russian Federation Abstract. Small mammals (rodents, insectivores, and bats) are the main reservoirs for a wide range of zoonotic viruses. These include the agents of vector-borne infections transmitted via bites of blood-sucking arthropods (ixodid ticks, mosquitoes, sand flies) and non-vector-borne infections (orthohantaviruses and others). Natural foci of viral infec­ tions, the reservoir of which are small mammals, are of primary epidemiological significance in the Russian Federation: hundreds of cases are recorded annually, many of which are severe. The aim of this review was to summarize current data on the circulation of viral zoonotic pathogens in small mammal populations in natural foci in the Russian Federation and worldwide, as well as to identify key issues in epizootiological surveillance and the study of reservoir relationships between hosts, pathogens, and vectors. It has been shown that among the zoonotic viruses circulating with the partici­ pation of rodents and insectivores, along with the most significant and widespread, returning (re-emerging) pathogens that pose a serious global and regional threat are also of great epidemiological importance. These are representatives of the Flaviviridae family (tick-borne encephalitis virus, Omsk hemorrhagic fever virus, Kyasanur forest disease virus), Bunyaviridae (orthohantaviruses, Crimean-Congo hemorrhagic fever virus, and others), and Coronaviridae families. It was noted that small mammals acted not only as reservoir hosts for viruses but also as feeders, ensuring the maintenance of populations of vectors (ixodid and argasid ticks, mosquitoes and midges), thereby creating stable parasitic systems. The issue of zoonotic viruses circulating among small mammals remains urgent for both the Russian Federation and 27 Problemy Osobo Opasnykh Infektsii [Problems of Particularly Dangerous Infections]. 2026; 3 Reviews В современном мире изучение популяций мел­ ких млекопитающих, являющихся природными ре­ зервуарами вирусных инфекций (носителями воз­ будителей природно-очаговых заболеваний и биоин­ дикаторами состояния окружающей среды), приоб­ ретает с каждым годом все большую значимость в экологии и медицине. Согласно K. Jones et al., среди всех событий воз­ никновения инфекционных заболеваний (EID events) зоонозы составляют 60,3 %. При этом 71,8 % зооноз­ ных EID events связаны с дикими животными [1]. По оценкам экспертов, именно дикая природа служит основным источником новых инфекционных угроз для человека, причем в подавляющем большинстве случаев резервуарами выступают мелкие млекопи­ тающие (грызуны, рукокрылые, насекомоядные), которые являются основными резервуарами значи­ тельного числа вирусных патогенов [2]. Высокая численность, синантропность мно­ гих видов и быстрая смена популяционных циклов делают мелких млекопитающих идеальными при­ родными резервуарами зоонозных патогенов. Так, пандемия COVID-19 наглядно продемонстрировала, что недооценка рисков, связанных с вирусами диких животных, может приводить к катастрофическим последствиям для человечества [3]. По состоянию на май 2026 г. в базе ZOVER со­ держится информация о данных секвенирования ге­ нов вирусов, ассоциированных с отрядом грызунов (Rodentia). Выявленные вирусы относятся к 36 се­ мействам. Основными носителями вирусов явля­ ются семейства мелких млекопитающих Muridae, Cricetidae и Sciuridae. Среди вирусов, выявленных у грызунов, наибольшее количество секвенирований генетических вариантов приходится на семейства Hantaviridae (5329; 30,5 %), Coronaviridae (1678; 9,6 %), Arenaviridae (1654; 9,5 %), Hepeviridae (1201; 6,9 %), Astroviridae (1079; 6,2 %), Paramyxoviridae (1058; 6,1 %), Picobirnaviridae (866; 5,0 %), Picorna­ viridae (853; 4,9 %), Anelloviridae (824; 4,7 %) и Flaviviridae (689; 3,9 %) [4]. При этом многие из этих семейств включают возбудителей, представляющих серьезную угрозу для общественного здравоохра­ нения. Значительным вирусным разнообразием харак­ теризуются также представители отряда рукокры­ лых (Chiroptera). База данных вирусов, ассоцииро­ ванных с летучими мышами, по состоянию на май 2026 г. содержит информацию о 27 233 сиквенсах вирусов, относящихся к 35 вирусным семействам. Наиболее значимыми из них являются Coronaviridae (11342; 46,9 %), Rhabdoviridae (3506; 14,5 %), Paramyxoviridae (2222; 9,2 %), Astroviridae (1575; 6,5 %), Adenoviridae (652; 2,7 %), Herpesviridae (558; 2,3 %), Picornaviridae (531; 2,2 %), Circoviridae (472; 2,0 %), Reoviridae (465; 1,9 %) и Polyomaviridae (359; 1,5 %) [4]. Отряд насекомоядных (Eulipotyphla) занимает третье место по численности среди отрядов млеко­ питающих, его представители являются значимым резервуаром вирусных патогенов. Согласно иссле­ дованию H. Li et al., насекомоядные являются хозяе­ вами для 941 микроорганизма, 60 % из которых со­ ставляют вирусы, преимущественно выявленные у представителей семейств землеройковых (Soricidae) и ежовых (Erinaceidae) [5]. Территория РФ характеризуется наличием мно­ гочисленных зоонозных природных очагов вирусных инфекций, что обусловлено разными ландшафтно- географическими зонами страны, видовым и чис­ ленным разнообразием животных-резервуаров. Мелкие млекопитающие представляют собой весьма обширную группу наземных позвоночных, распро­ страненных повсеместно. Они хорошо адаптирова­ ны к различным типам среды обитания и являются связующим звеном между естественными и антро­ погенными экосистемами. На энзоотичных по различным инфекциям тер­ риториях отдельные виды диких мелких млекопи­ тающих могут иметь важное эпидемиологическое значение из-за тесного контакта с человеком. Во многих случаях наблюдается сочетание природных очагов разных инфекционных агентов не только в результате их территориального совмещения, но и the global community. Analysis of global trends indicates that infectious diseases of animals are expanding their range, thereat many of them with zoonotic potential. The key drivers of this process are climate change, expansion of interna­ tional trade and transformation of ecosystems, requiring improved epidemiological monitoring and an interdisciplinary approach to risk assessment. Дикие мелкие млекопитающие, главным об­ разом грызуны, играют центральную роль в поддер­ жании природных очагов трансмиссивных вирусных инфекций. Они выступают в качестве резервуара ви­ руса, в котором происходит его репликация и сохра­ нение в популяции, а также являются прокормите­ лями кровососущих членистоногих – переносчиков инфекций (клещей, комаров и блох). В последние годы наблюдается тенденция к рас­ ширению ареалов иксодовых клещей-переносчиков, что связывают с изменением экологических условий и трансформацией экосистем [7, 8]. В ряде регионов документировано выявление устойчивых популяций клещей за пределами их известных ареалов, а также новые виды животных-прокормителей, что может играть важную роль в распространении «клещевых» инфекций [8]. Питаясь кровью млекопитающих, клещи могут инфицироваться (виремическая транс­ миссия) на любой постэмбриональной стадии своего развития. В фазе развития личинки и нимфы клещи в основном питаются на мелких грызунах или птицах, взрослые особи – на более крупных позвоночных. В качестве прокормителей клещей в распростране­ нии очагов клещевых инфекций важное значение имеют представители многих семейств млекопи­ тающих и птиц. Ключевую роль играют грызуны (включая семейства Muridae, Cricetidae, Sciuridae и др.), насекомоядные (Eulipotyphla), зайцеобразные (Leporidae), а также различные виды птиц, особенно из семейства врановых (Corvidae) отряда воробьи­ нообразных (Passeriformes) и других наземно- кормящихся, которые не только служат источником питания, но и способствуют распространению кле­ щей. Взрослые стадии клещей часто предпочита­ ют крупных млекопитающих, таких как копытные (Artiodactyla) и хищные (Carnivora) [9, 10]. Среди возбудителей природно-очаговых инфек­ ций, регистрация которых в последнее время растет, особое место занимают ортохантавирусы – классиче­ ские зоонозные патогены, ассоциированные с опре­ деленными видами мелких млекопитающих (рыжая, красно-серая, обыкновенная, большая полевки, по­ левая, восточноазиатская, кавказская мыши, серая крыса) [11]. Согласно последнему таксономическо­ му обзору, род Orthohantavirus относится к подсе­ мейству Mammantavirinae, семейству Hantaviridae, порядку Elliovirales и включает в себя более 30 раз­ личных вирусов [12]. Хантавирусы являются классическими пред­ ставителями возбудителей природно-очаговых зоо­ нозных инфекций, циркулирующих в популяциях мелких млекопитающих. В отличие от трансмис­ сивных арбовирусов, они не требуют переносчиков- членистоногих и передаются человеку преимуще­ ственно аэрогенным путем при контакте с экскре­ тами инфицированных грызунов. Важно отметить, что для данных вирусов характерна бессимптомная персистенция в организме хозяина, который выде­ ляет вирус в окружающую среду с мочой, калом и слюной [13]. В систематическом обзоре D. Fabbri et. al. обоб­ щены современные данные о комплексе экологи­ ческих факторов (популяционная динамика хозя­ ев, структура сообществ, климатические условия), определяющих распространенность хантавирусов у мелких млекопитающих. На примере хантавиру­ сов Европы показано, что их распространенность в популяциях мелких млекопитающих определяется комплексом экологических факторов: популяцион­ ными циклами хозяев, структурой сообществ, кли­ матическими условиями и абиотическими факто­ рами. Авторы подчеркивают, что, несмотря на зна­ чительный прогресс в изучении этих взаимосвязей, сохраняется ряд ключевых нерешенных вопросов, что затрудняет точную оценку рисков для здоровья человека [14]. Хантавирусы вызывают тяжелые заболевания человека (геморрагическую лихорадку с почеч­ ным синдромом в Евразии и хантавирусный кар­ диопульмональный синдром в Северной и Южной Америке) [13]. Филогенетический анализ демон­ стрирует тесную коэволюцию вирусов с их хозяе­ вами: вирусы формируют обособленные кластеры в зависимости от принадлежности к подсемей­ ствам грызунов Murinae, Arvicolinae, Neotominae и Sigmodontinae [15–17]. В Российской Федерации геморрагическая лихорадка с почечным синдромом (ГЛПС) остает­ ся одной из самых распространенных природно- очаговых вирусных инфекций. С момента выявления ГЛПС с 1978 по 2023 г. в России зарегистрировано 297 172 случая, за 2024 г. – 3396, за 2025 г. – 4912 [18, 19]. По данным Роспотребнадзора за 2025 г., в Приволжском федеральном округе сосредоточено более 80 % от всех случаев ГЛПС в РФ [19]. Этиологическая структура ГЛПС в России пред­ ставлена шестью типами хантавирусов: Hantaan, Amur, Seoul, Puumala, Kurkino и Sochi. Для Hantaan, Amur, Seoul и Puumala достоверно установлена ассо­ циация с определенными видами-резервуарами из се­ мейств мышиных (Muridae) и хомяковых (Cricetidae) [11, 20]. Однако для вирусов Kurkino и Sochi эти данные требуют дальнейшего подтверждения ввиду ограниченного числа находок. Кроме того, в России выявлены и другие хантавирусы (Adler, Khabarovsk, Taimyr), ассоциация которых с резервуарами пока носит предварительный характер. Среди хантавирусов, циркулирующих на тер­ ритории России, наиболее изученным является ви­ рус Puumala, персистирующий в популяциях рыжей полевки (Myodes glareolus) и выступающий основ­ ным этиологическим агентом ГЛПС в европей­ ской части страны. На юге России с мышами рода Apodemus ассоциированы вирусы Dobrava/Belgrad (генотипы Kurkino и Sochi), с кустарниковой по­ левкой (Microtus majori) – вид Adler. На полуострове Таймыр от сибир­ ских леммингов (Lemmus sibiricus) выделен вид Taimyr [11]. Важно отметить, что 97,7 % случаев ГЛПС в России вызываются вирусом Puumala и лишь 2,3 % приходится на остальные типы хантавирусов. Однако отмечается низкая эффективность их выде­ ления [11]. Многолетние исследования в Калужской обла­ сти (1993–2019 гг.) показали, что основными носи­ телями хантавирусов в луго-полевых стациях явля­ ются серые полевки (Microtus spp.) и полевая мышь (Apodemus agrarius). Вялых1 Возбудители зоонозных вирусных инфекций, циркулирующие в популяциях мелких млекопитающих: обзор современного состояния 1Федеральный научно-исследовательский институт вирусных инфекций «Виром», Екатеринбург, Российская Федерация; 2Уральский федеральный аграрный научно-исследовательский центр Уральского отделения Российской академии наук, Екатеринбург, Российская Федерация; 3Институт экологии растений и животных Уральского отделения Российской академии наук, Екатеринбург, Российская Федерация Мелкие млекопитающие (грызуны, насекомоядные, рукокрылые) являются основными резервуарами широко­ го спектра зоонозных вирусов, включая как возбудителей трансмиссивных инфекций, передающихся через укусы кровососущих членистоногих (иксодовые клещи, комары, москиты), так и другими путями передачи (ортоханта­ вирусы и др.). На территории Российской Федерации природные очаги вирусных инфекций, резервуаром которых являются мелкие млекопитающие, имеют значительное эпидемиологическое значение – ежегодно регистрируют­ ся сотни случаев заболеваний, многие из которых протекают в тяжелой форме. Целью обзора являлось обобще­ ние современных данных о циркуляции вирусных зоонозных патогенов в популяциях мелких млекопитающих в природных очагах РФ и мира, а также выявление ключевых проблем эпизоотологического надзора и изуче­ ние резервуарных взаимоотношений между хозяевами, возбудителями и переносчиками. Показано, что среди зоонозных вирусов, циркулирующих с участием грызунов и насекомоядных, наряду с наиболее значимыми и широко распространенными, важное эпидемиологическое значение имеют и возвращающиеся (re-emerging) пато­ гены, представляющие серьезную глобальную и региональную угрозу. Это представители семейств Flaviviridae (вирус клещевого энцефалита, вирус омской геморрагической лихорадки, вирус Киасанурской лесной болезни), Bunyaviridae (ортохантавирусы, вирус Крымской-Конго геморрагической лихорадки и др.), Coronaviridae и про­ чих. Отмечено, что мелкие млекопитающие выступают не только в качестве резервуарных хозяев для вирусов, но и как прокормители, обеспечивающие поддержание и рост популяций переносчиков (иксодовых и аргасовых кле­ щей, комаров, москитов), что создает устойчивые паразитарные системы. Проблема зоонозных вирусов, цирку­ лирующих среди мелких млекопитающих, остается остроактуальной как для РФ, так и для мирового сообщества. Анализ глобальных тенденций показывает, что инфекционные болезни животных расширяют свой ареал, причем многие из них обладают зооантропонозным потенциалом. Ключевыми драйверами этого процесса выступают изменение климата, расширение международной торговли и трансформация экосистем, что требует совершен­ ствования эпидемиологического мониторинга и междисциплинарного подхода к оценке рисков. Ключевые слова: мелкие млекопитающие, зоонозы, трансмиссивные инфекции, природные очаги, Bunyaviridae, Flaviviridae, Coronaviridae. Vyalykh1 Pathogens of Zoonotic Viral Infections, Circulating in Populations of Small Mammals: an Overview of the Current State 1Federal Research Institute of Viral Infections “Virom”, Yekaterinburg, Russian Federation; 2Ural Federal Agrarian Research Center of the Ural Branch of the Russian Academy of Sciences, Yekaterinburg, Russian Federation; 3Institute of Plant and Animal Ecology of the Ural Branch of the Russian Academy of Sciences, Ekaterinburg, Russian Federation Abstract. Small mammals (rodents, insectivores, and bats) are the main reservoirs for a wide range of zoonotic viruses. These include the agents of vector-borne infections transmitted via bites of blood-sucking arthropods (ixodid ticks, mosquitoes, sand flies) and non-vector-borne infections (orthohantaviruses and others). Natural foci of viral infec­ tions, the reservoir of which are small mammals, are of primary epidemiological significance in the Russian Federation: hundreds of cases are recorded annually, many of which are severe. The aim of this review was to summarize current data on the circulation of viral zoonotic pathogens in small mammal populations in natural foci in the Russian Federation and worldwide, as well as to identify key issues in epizootiological surveillance and the study of reservoir relationships between hosts, pathogens, and vectors. It has been shown that among the zoonotic viruses circulating with the partici­ pation of rodents and insectivores, along with the most significant and widespread, returning (re-emerging) pathogens that pose a serious global and regional threat are also of great epidemiological importance. These are representatives of the Flaviviridae family (tick-borne encephalitis virus, Omsk hemorrhagic fever virus, Kyasanur forest disease virus), Bunyaviridae (orthohantaviruses, Crimean-Congo hemorrhagic fever virus, and others), and Coronaviridae families. It was noted that small mammals acted not only as reservoir hosts for viruses but also as feeders, ensuring the maintenance of populations of vectors (ixodid and argasid ticks, mosquitoes and midges), thereby creating stable parasitic systems. Согласно K. Jones et al., среди всех событий воз­ никновения инфекционных заболеваний (EID events) зоонозы составляют 60,3 %. При этом 71,8 % зооноз­ ных EID events связаны с дикими животными [1]. По оценкам экспертов, именно дикая природа служит основным источником новых инфекционных угроз для человека, причем в подавляющем большинстве случаев резервуарами выступают мелкие млекопи­ тающие (грызуны, рукокрылые, насекомоядные), которые являются основными резервуарами значи­ тельного числа вирусных патогенов [2]. Высокая численность, синантропность мно­ гих видов и быстрая смена популяционных циклов делают мелких млекопитающих идеальными при­ родными резервуарами зоонозных патогенов. papers.title_zh: 小型哺乳动物种群中循环的动物源性病毒病原体:现状概览

analysis_zh.background: 小型哺乳动物是多种动物源性病毒的主要宿主,包括媒介传播和非媒介传播的病原体,俄罗斯的自然疫源地每年导致数百例重症病例,凸显该问题在全球范围的紧迫性。
analysis_zh.methods: 本综述汇总了俄罗斯及全球自然疫源地小型哺乳动物种群中动物源性病毒病原体循环的最新数据,并指出流行病学监测和宿主关系中的关键问题。
analysis_zh.results: 综述发现了在循环中的病毒,分别属于黄病毒科(蜱媒脑炎、Omsk出血热、Kyasanur森林病)、布尼亚病毒科(正汉坦病毒es、克里米亚-刚果出血热)以及冠状病毒科,并指出小型哺乳动物既是宿主也是为媒介种群提供血源的供体,形成稳定的寄生系统。
analysis_zh.contribution: 本文强调小型哺乳动物宿主的流行病学重要性,突出再现性病原体对全球和地区构成的威胁,并强调亟需加强监测和跨学科风险评估。
analysis_zh.limitations: 未在提供的证据中报告。

papers.title: The Potential Risk Factors of Hantavirus Transmission to Humans from Infected Rodents in Malaysia
papers.abstract: Zoonotic hantavirus is a negative single-stranded RNA virus from the family Bunyaviridae which is known to cause two significant rodent-borne diseases in humans namely hemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome (HFRS) and hantavirus pulmonary syndrome (HPS), affecting about 30 000 people worldwide each year. HFRS is a disease found endemically in Asia and Europe with case fatality rates varying from <1% to 12%, while HPS which has a higher mortality rate of approximately 40% occurs within the American continent. Many countries in Southeast Asia unaware the public health implication of Hantavirus infection despite favorable ecological conditions include rich rodent species diversity, urbanisation and high human-wildlife interface that serve as ecological condition that could support the virus persistence and transmission.Since humans serve as spillover hosts who are infected largely by inhalation of infected rodents’ excreta, it is crucial to fill in the research gap by identifying the risk factors for human hantavirus infection. This paper provides a review of the potential risk factors associated with hantavirus transmission to humans from infected rodents in Malaysia focusing on behavioral, occupational, urban, and environmental. Other pieces of knowledge such as hantavirus virological properties, the geographical distribution with its respective role as a reservoir, clinical features, and diagnostic challenges, particularly its propensity to be misclassified due to mimic symptom with dengue and leptospirosis. To effectively mitigate transmission, Malaysia must transition from a fragmented surveillance model to a proactive, integrated One Health framework that bridges the inter-governmental agencies through a unified data-sharing platform to monitor active viral strains and prevent localised spillover outbreaks.
papers.journal: Pertanika Journal of Veterinary Medicine and Science

HFRS is a disease found endemically in Asia and Europe with case fatality rates varying from <1% to 12%, while HPS which has a higher mortality rate of approximately 40% occurs within the American continent. Many countries in Southeast Asia unaware the public health implication of Hantavirus infection despite favorable ecological conditions include rich rodent species diversity, urbanisation and high human-wildlife interface that serve as ecological condition that could support the virus persistence and transmission.Since humans serve as spillover hosts who are infected largely by inhalation of infected rodents’ excreta, it is crucial to fill in the research gap by identifying the risk factors for human hantavirus infection. This paper provides a review of the potential risk factors associated with hantavirus transmission to humans from infected rodents in Malaysia focusing on behavioral, occupational, urban, and environmental. Other pieces of knowledge such as hantavirus virological properties, the geographical distribution with its respective role as a reservoir, clinical features, and diagnostic challenges, particularly its propensity to be misclassified due to mimic symptom with dengue and leptospirosis. To effectively mitigate transmission, Malaysia must transition from a fragmented surveillance model to a proactive, integrated One Health framework that bridges the inter-governmental agencies through a unified data-sharing platform to monitor active viral strains and prevent localised spillover outbreaks.
source_records.journal: Pertanika Journal of Veterinary Medicine and Science

papers.title: In Silico Prediction and Structural Mapping of Linear B-Cell Epitopes in Andes Virus Glycoprotein as Potential Vaccine Candidates
papers.abstract: Andes virus (ANDV), a pathogenic orthohantavirus associated with hantavirus cardiopulmonary syndrome, remains a public health concern because of its severe clinical outcomes and the absence of broadly approved vaccines for human use. The viral glycoprotein is a relevant antigenic target because of its surface localization and role in viral entry. This study aimed to identify and structurally map linear B-cell epitope candidates in the Andes virus glycoprotein using an immunoinformatics-based approach. The ANDV glycoprotein sequence was retrieved from UniProt, and linear B-cell epitopes were predicted using BepiPred 3.0 with a threshold of 0.030. Candidate peptides were further evaluated for antigenicity, allergenicity, and toxicity using VaxiJen v2.0, AllerTOP v2.1, and ToxinPred, respectively. The three-dimensional glycoprotein model was generated using AlphaFold, refined with GalaxyWEB, and validated using ERRAT and Ramachandran plot analysis. Five preliminary epitope candidates were identified, among which E1, E2, E3, and E4 met the antigenicity criterion. The refined structure showed favorable validation parameters, with an ERRAT score of 97.73 and 97.88% of residues in the favored Ramachandran region. Structural mapping indicated that E1 (EWRKKSDTTDTTNAASTTFE) and E2 (QTKTVNLRGT) were positioned on exposed surface regions, supporting their prioritization as the most promising candidates. E4 (PSTSSTDT) also showed potential, whereas E3 (HPRGEDHD), despite having the highest antigenicity score, appeared less structurally exposed. These findings provide preliminary computational evidence for surface-accessible linear B-cell epitope candidates in ANDV glycoprotein. However, experimental validation is required to confirm their immunological relevance.

papers.full_text: Volume 1 (2026) h/ps://doi.org/10.22452/jtoh.vol1.7 SHORT COMMUNICATION Published by Tropical Infec5ous Disease Research and Educa5on Centre (TIDREC), Universi5 Malaya In Silico Prediction and Structural Mapping of Candidate Linear B-Cell Epitopes in Andes Virus Glycoprotein Husaina Kunii Nariswari1, Moh. Royhan Afnani1,3, Muhammad Fajrul Adi Syahputra1, Rangga Adhi Prastika2,3, Abdul Rahman Siregar1* 1Department of Biology, Faculty of Biology, Universitas Gadjah Mada, Yogyakarta, 55281, Indonesia 2Department of Nanotechnology Engineering, Faculty of Advanced Technology and Multidiscipline, Universitas Airlangga, Surabaya 60115, Indonesia. 3Drug and Vaccine Innovation Research Group, Virtual Research Center for Bioinformatics and Biotechnology, Surabaya, Indonesia *Corresponding author: ar.siregar@ugm.ac.id ARTICLE HISTORY Received: 16 Jun 2026 Revised: 21 Jul 2026 Accepted: 29 Jul 2026 Published: 30 Sep 2026 ABSTRACT Andes virus (ANDV), a pathogenic orthohantavirus associated with hantavirus cardiopulmonary syndrome, remains a public health concern because of its severe clinical outcomes and the absence of broadly approved vaccines for human use. The viral glycoprotein is a relevant antigenic target because of its surface localization and role in viral entry. This study aimed to identify and prioritize candidate linear B-cell epitopes in the ANDV glycoprotein using an integrated immunoinformatics approach. The ANDV glycoprotein sequence was retrieved from UniProt, and linear B-cell epitopes were predicted using BepiPred 3.0 with a threshold of 0.030. Candidate peptides were evaluated for antigenicity, allergenicity, and toxicity using VaxiJen v2.0, AllerTOP v2.1, and ToxinPred, respectively. The three-dimensional glycoprotein model was generated using AlphaFold, refined with GalaxyWEB, and validated using ERRAT and Ramachandran plot analysis. Surface-localized candidates were further assessed through molecular docking with a B-cell receptor structure using ClusPro 2.0, followed by binding free energy estimation using PRODIGY. E1 (EWRKKSDTTDTTNAASTTFE), E2 (QTKTVNLRGT), and E4 (PSTSSTDT) showed favorable antigenicity, non-allergenic and non-toxic profiles, and surface localization on the glycoprotein model. Docking analysis further supported their prioritization, with predicted binding free energies of -10.0, -9.4, and -9.1 kcal/mol for E1, E2, and E4, respectively. Overall, E1 emerged as the strongest candidate, while E2 and E4 represent additional candidates for further validation. These findings provide preliminary computational evidence for candidate linear B-cell epitopes in ANDV glycoprotein, although experimental confirmation remains necessary. Keywords: Andes virus; B-cell epitope; glycoprotein; immunoinformatics; structural mapping; candidate linear B-cell epitope Introduction A recent cluster of Andes virus infections associated with the cruise ship MV Hondius has heightened international concern regarding the public health significance of pathogenic orthohantaviruses (Koopmans et al., 2026). Andes virus (ANDV), a zoonotic pathogen within the genus Orthohantavirus and family Hantaviridae, typically infects humans through inhalation of aerosolized particles contaminated with urine, feces, or saliva from infected rodent reservoirs. Notably, ANDV is epidemiologically unique due to documented instances of limited person-to- person transmission, particularly among close contacts (Chediack et al., 2026; Martinez- Valdebenito et al., 2014). This transmission feature, combined with its association with severe cardiopulmonary disease, underscores the importance of ANDV for public health surveillance, outbreak preparedness, and vaccine development. ANDV is a primary etiological agent of hantavirus Journal of Tropical One Health Volume 1 (2026) Nariswari et al. h/ps://doi.org/10.22452/jtoh.vol1.1 Published by Tropical Infec5ous Disease Research and Educa5on Centre (TIDREC), Universi5 Malaya cardiopulmonary syndrome (HCPS), a severe disease marked by increased pulmonary vascular permeability, pulmonary edema, acute respiratory failure, and cardiogenic shock (Warner et al., 2025). While the incidence of HCPS is generally lower than that of hemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome caused by Old World hantaviruses, HCPS exhibits a substantially higher case-fatality rate, typically reported at 30–40% (Angulo et al., 2017; Barrera et al., 2025; Quarleri et al., 2026). Despite the clinical severity of ANDV infection, no specific antiviral therapy or widely approved vaccine is currently available for human use. This lack of medical countermeasures is particularly concerning given ecological disturbances, climate variability, and habitat changes that may influence rodent population dynamics and elevate the risk of human exposure to infected reservoirs (Moirano et al., 2024). Structurally, ANDV is an enveloped, negative- sense RNA virus with a tripartite genome consisting of small, medium, and large segments. The small segment encodes the nucleocapsid protein, the medium segment encodes a glycoprotein precursor processed into Gn and Gc, and the large segment encodes the RNA- dependent RNA polymerase (Beltrán-Ortiz et al., 2017). The envelope glycoproteins Gn and Gc are of particular interest for vaccine development because they are displayed on the virion surface and mediate host-cell attachment, receptor engagement, endocytic entry, and membrane fusion. Their surface exposure facilitates antibody recognition, supporting their selection as antigenic targets for epitope-based vaccine research (Banerjee & Mukhopadhyay, 2016; Cifuentes-Muñoz et al., 2014). B-cell epitopes are specific antigenic regions recognized by antibodies and contribute to humoral immune responses (Caoili, 2022). In vaccine design, identifying B-cell epitopes is essential because antibody-mediated immunity and immunological memory are critical for protection against viral reinfection. Linear B-cell epitopes are particularly valuable in immunoinformatics-based screening, as they can be derived from the primary amino acid sequence, assessed for antigenicity and safety, and mapped onto three-dimensional antigen structures (Riswana & Punjungsari, 2025). However, sequence-based prediction alone does not adequately determine biological accessibility or immunogenic potential. Structural mapping is therefore required to establish whether predicted epitopes are located on solvent-exposed regions of the target protein, where they are more likely to be accessible to antibody binding (Afnani & Purnama, 2025; Francino-Urdaniz & Whitehead, 2021). Although B-cell epitope prediction, multiepitope vaccine design, and structural evaluation have been applied in viral vaccine- related studies, including hantavirus targets, most previous hantavirus immunoinformatics studies have emphasized broad whole-proteome screening or multiepitope vaccine construct design rather than a focused prioritization of linear B-cell epitopes derived specifically from the ANDV glycoprotein (Abdulla et al., 2021). The novelty of the present study therefore does not rely on the use of individual computational tools, which are well-established in immunoinformatics research, but on the ANDV- specific integration of linear B-cell epitope prediction, antigenicity and safety screening, three-dimensional structural mapping, and molecular docking with a B-cell receptor structure for candidate prioritization. This integrated approach allows predicted epitopes to be evaluated not only on the basis of sequence-level epitope propensity, but also according to their predicted antigenicity, safety profile, structural localization, and interaction potential with an antigen-recognition model. Such a focused framework is particularly relevant for glycoprotein antigens, in which not all sequence- predicted epitopes are necessarily exposed or available for antibody recognition on the folded protein surface. Therefore, this study aimed to identify and prioritize linear B-cell epitope candidates in the Andes virus glycoprotein through an integrated immunoinformatics approach combining sequence-based prediction, antigenicity and safety screening, three-dimensional structural mapping, and molecular docking with a B-cell receptor structure. Candidate epitopes were further assessed for antigenicity, allergenicity, toxicity, structural localization, and predicted BCR-binding affinity. The results provide preliminary computational evidence for prioritized surface-accessible linear B-cell epitope candidates that may inform future experimental evaluation for Andes virus vaccine-associated or diagnostic applications. However, as this study is Journal of Tropical One Health Volume 1 (2026) Nariswari et al. h/ps://doi.org/10.22452/jtoh.vol1.1 Published by Tropical Infec5ous Disease Research and Educa5on Centre (TIDREC), Universi5 Malaya entirely computational, the predicted epitopes should be regarded as potential candidates requiring further experimental validation through in vitro and in vivo studies. Materials and Methods Retrieval and Curation of Andes Virus Glycoprotein Sequence The ANDV glycoprotein sequence was retrieved from the UniProt Knowledgebase using the taxonomic identifier and protein accession as search criteria. The UniProt entry Q9E006, annotated as ANDV glycoprotein and consisting of 1138 amino acids, was selected as the reference sequence for downstream analysis (Shimizu et al., 2013). The FASTA sequence and associated metadata, including accession number, organism name, protein length, and database source, were recorded to ensure sequence traceability and reproducibility. UniProtKB provides curated protein sequence and functional annotation resources, supporting its use as a primary source for protein sequence retrieval. Linear B-Cell Epitope Prediction Linear B-cell epitope prediction was performed using BepiPred 3.0, a sequence-based epitope prediction tool developed for identifying residues with potential B-cell epitope propensity (Clifford et al., 2022). The higher-confidence prediction option was selected. In this study, a threshold of ≥0.030 was used as a sequence-specific operational cutoff based on the score distribution observed across the ANDV glycoprotein. This cutoff was selected to balance epitope recovery and prediction stringency. Higher cutoff values retained only a very limited number of short epitope regions and reduced the ability to capture biologically plausible contiguous peptide segments, whereas lower cutoff values increased the inclusion of low-scoring regions that may represent less reliable predictions. Antigenicity, Allergenicity, and Toxicity Screening The predicted linear B-cell epitope candidates were further evaluated for antigenicity, allergenicity, and toxicity. Antigenicity was assessed using VaxiJen v2.0 with a threshold value of 0.400; peptides with antigenicity scores above this threshold were considered potentially antigenic (Afnani, Kharisma, et al., 2026). VaxiJen is an alignment-independent antigen prediction server that classifies antigens based on the physicochemical properties of protein sequences (Doytchinova & Flower, 2007). Allergenicity was predicted using AllerTOP v2.1, and only peptides classified as non-allergenic were retained. AllerTOP is an alignment-free allergenicity prediction server based on physicochemical properties and machine-learning classification (Dimitrov et al., 2014). Toxicity was evaluated using ToxinPred, and peptides predicted as non-toxic were prioritized for further structural mapping. ToxinPred is designed to classify peptides as toxic or non-toxic based on computational sequence-derived features (Rathore et al., 2024). Prediction, Refinement, and 3D Structure Validation The three-dimensional (3D) structure of the Andes virus glycoprotein was predicted using the AlphaFold Server (Kovalevskiy et al., 2024; Prastika et al., 2026). The predicted structure was then refined using the GalaxyWEB server to improve local structural geometry and reduce potential modeling artifacts. The refined model was validated using structure quality assessment parameters (Ko et al., 2012). The ERRAT score was calculated using the Structure Validation Server, and stereochemical quality was assessed using Ramachandran plot analysis through RamPlot (Afnani, Emilia, et al., 2026; Laskowski et al., 2013). The validated model was subsequently used as the structural template for mapping the selected linear B-cell epitope candidates. Structural Mapping and Visualization of Linear B-Cell Epitope Candidates The selected linear B-cell epitope candidates were mapped onto the refined 3D structure of the ANDV glycoprotein using PyMOL under an academic license. Epitope positions were identified based on their amino acid coordinates in the full-length glycoprotein sequence and visualized on the 3D model using distinct colors. Both cartoon and surface representations were generated to assess the spatial distribution and surface exposure of each candidate epitope (Riswana & Punjungsari, 2025). Epitope candidates located on surface-exposed regions were prioritized because B-cell epitopes are more likely to be accessible to antibody recognition when positioned on the external surface of the antigen. In contrast, epitopes located within Journal of Tropical One Health Volume 1 (2026) Nariswari et al. h/ps://doi.org/10.22452/jtoh.vol1.1 Published by Tropical Infec5ous Disease Research and Educa5on Centre (TIDREC), Universi5 Malaya buried, transmembrane, or structurally uncertain regions were interpreted with caution and were not prioritized for further analysis. Molecular Docking with B-Cell ReceptorThe prioritized linear B-cell epitopes, were further evaluated through molecular docking with the B- cell receptor (BCR). The BCR structure was obtained from the RCSB Protein Data Bank using PDB ID 5IFH (Riswana & Punjungsari, 2025). Molecular docking was performed using the ClusPro 2.0, with BCR designated as the receptor and each epitope peptide as the ligand (Arapa et al., 2026). The best-ranked docking complex from each epitope-BCR interaction was selected for further evaluation. The predicted binding free energy (ΔG) of each complex was then assessed using the PRODIGY web server, where more negative ΔG values indicate stronger predicted binding affinity (Xue et al., 2016). The resulting docking complexes were visualized using PyMOL to examine the interaction orientation and spatial positioning of each epitope on the BCR surface. This analysis is significant because B-cell epitopes represent antigenic regions recognized by antibodies and may serve as preliminary targets for vaccine- associated evaluation, immunodiagnostic development, and immune-reactivity assessment. full_text_sections.full_text: Volume 1 (2026) h/ps://doi.org/10.22452/jtoh.vol1.7 SHORT COMMUNICATION Published by Tropical Infec5ous Disease Research and Educa5on Centre (TIDREC), Universi5 Malaya In Silico Prediction and Structural Mapping of Candidate Linear B-Cell Epitopes in Andes Virus Glycoprotein Husaina Kunii Nariswari1, Moh. Royhan Afnani1,3, Muhammad Fajrul Adi Syahputra1, Rangga Adhi Prastika2,3, Abdul Rahman Siregar1* 1Department of Biology, Faculty of Biology, Universitas Gadjah Mada, Yogyakarta, 55281, Indonesia 2Department of Nanotechnology Engineering, Faculty of Advanced Technology and Multidiscipline, Universitas Airlangga, Surabaya 60115, Indonesia. 3Drug and Vaccine Innovation Research Group, Virtual Research Center for Bioinformatics and Biotechnology, Surabaya, Indonesia *Corresponding author: ar.siregar@ugm.ac.id ARTICLE HISTORY Received: 16 Jun 2026 Revised: 21 Jul 2026 Accepted: 29 Jul 2026 Published: 30 Sep 2026 ABSTRACT Andes virus (ANDV), a pathogenic orthohantavirus associated with hantavirus cardiopulmonary syndrome, remains a public health concern because of its severe clinical outcomes and the absence of broadly approved vaccines for human use. The viral glycoprotein is a relevant antigenic target because of its surface localization and role in viral entry. This study aimed to identify and prioritize candidate linear B-cell epitopes in the ANDV glycoprotein using an integrated immunoinformatics approach. The ANDV glycoprotein sequence was retrieved from UniProt, and linear B-cell epitopes were predicted using BepiPred 3.0 with a threshold of 0.030. Candidate peptides were evaluated for antigenicity, allergenicity, and toxicity using VaxiJen v2.0, AllerTOP v2.1, and ToxinPred, respectively. The three-dimensional glycoprotein model was generated using AlphaFold, refined with GalaxyWEB, and validated using ERRAT and Ramachandran plot analysis. Surface-localized candidates were further assessed through molecular docking with a B-cell receptor structure using ClusPro 2.0, followed by binding free energy estimation using PRODIGY. E1 (EWRKKSDTTDTTNAASTTFE), E2 (QTKTVNLRGT), and E4 (PSTSSTDT) showed favorable antigenicity, non-allergenic and non-toxic profiles, and surface localization on the glycoprotein model. Docking analysis further supported their prioritization, with predicted binding free energies of -10.0, -9.4, and -9.1 kcal/mol for E1, E2, and E4, respectively. Overall, E1 emerged as the strongest candidate, while E2 and E4 represent additional candidates for further validation. These findings provide preliminary computational evidence for candidate linear B-cell epitopes in ANDV glycoprotein, although experimental confirmation remains necessary. Keywords: Andes virus; B-cell epitope; glycoprotein; immunoinformatics; structural mapping; candidate linear B-cell epitope Introduction A recent cluster of Andes virus infections associated with the cruise ship MV Hondius has heightened international concern regarding the public health significance of pathogenic orthohantaviruses (Koopmans et al., 2026). Andes virus (ANDV), a zoonotic pathogen within the genus Orthohantavirus and family Hantaviridae, typically infects humans through inhalation of aerosolized particles contaminated with urine, feces, or saliva from infected rodent reservoirs. Notably, ANDV is epidemiologically unique due to documented instances of limited person-to- person transmission, particularly among close contacts (Chediack et al., 2026; Martinez- Valdebenito et al., 2014). This transmission feature, combined with its association with severe cardiopulmonary disease, underscores the importance of ANDV for public health surveillance, outbreak preparedness, and vaccine development. ANDV is a primary etiological agent of hantavirus Journal of Tropical One Health Volume 1 (2026) Nariswari et al. h/ps://doi.org/10.22452/jtoh.vol1.1 Published by Tropical Infec5ous Disease Research and Educa5on Centre (TIDREC), Universi5 Malaya cardiopulmonary syndrome (HCPS), a severe disease marked by increased pulmonary vascular permeability, pulmonary edema, acute respiratory failure, and cardiogenic shock (Warner et al., 2025). While the incidence of HCPS is generally lower than that of hemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome caused by Old World hantaviruses, HCPS exhibits a substantially higher case-fatality rate, typically reported at 30–40% (Angulo et al., 2017; Barrera et al., 2025; Quarleri et al., 2026). Despite the clinical severity of ANDV infection, no specific antiviral therapy or widely approved vaccine is currently available for human use. This lack of medical countermeasures is particularly concerning given ecological disturbances, climate variability, and habitat changes that may influence rodent population dynamics and elevate the risk of human exposure to infected reservoirs (Moirano et al., 2024). Structurally, ANDV is an enveloped, negative- sense RNA virus with a tripartite genome consisting of small, medium, and large segments. The small segment encodes the nucleocapsid protein, the medium segment encodes a glycoprotein precursor processed into Gn and Gc, and the large segment encodes the RNA- dependent RNA polymerase (Beltrán-Ortiz et al., 2017). The envelope glycoproteins Gn and Gc are of particular interest for vaccine development because they are displayed on the virion surface and mediate host-cell attachment, receptor engagement, endocytic entry, and membrane fusion. Their surface exposure facilitates antibody recognition, supporting their selection as antigenic targets for epitope-based vaccine research (Banerjee & Mukhopadhyay, 2016; Cifuentes-Muñoz et al., 2014). B-cell epitopes are specific antigenic regions recognized by antibodies and contribute to humoral immune responses (Caoili, 2022). In vaccine design, identifying B-cell epitopes is essential because antibody-mediated immunity and immunological memory are critical for protection against viral reinfection. Linear B-cell epitopes are particularly valuable in immunoinformatics-based screening, as they can be derived from the primary amino acid sequence, assessed for antigenicity and safety, and mapped onto three-dimensional antigen structures (Riswana & Punjungsari, 2025). However, sequence-based prediction alone does not adequately determine biological accessibility or immunogenic potential. Structural mapping is therefore required to establish whether predicted epitopes are located on solvent-exposed regions of the target protein, where they are more likely to be accessible to antibody binding (Afnani & Purnama, 2025; Francino-Urdaniz & Whitehead, 2021). Although B-cell epitope prediction, multiepitope vaccine design, and structural evaluation have been applied in viral vaccine- related studies, including hantavirus targets, most previous hantavirus immunoinformatics studies have emphasized broad whole-proteome screening or multiepitope vaccine construct design rather than a focused prioritization of linear B-cell epitopes derived specifically from the ANDV glycoprotein (Abdulla et al., 2021). The novelty of the present study therefore does not rely on the use of individual computational tools, which are well-established in immunoinformatics research, but on the ANDV- specific integration of linear B-cell epitope prediction, antigenicity and safety screening, three-dimensional structural mapping, and molecular docking with a B-cell receptor structure for candidate prioritization. This integrated approach allows predicted epitopes to be evaluated not only on the basis of sequence-level epitope propensity, but also according to their predicted antigenicity, safety profile, structural localization, and interaction potential with an antigen-recognition model. Such a focused framework is particularly relevant for glycoprotein antigens, in which not all sequence- predicted epitopes are necessarily exposed or available for antibody recognition on the folded protein surface. papers.title: Transmisión interpersonal del virus Andes: revisión narrativa de la evidencia actual y sus implicaciones clínicas
papers.abstract: Los hantavirus constituyen un grupo de virus responsables de zoonosis emergentes transmitidas principalmente por roedores. El virus Andes (ANDV), endémico de Sudamérica, constituye una excepción dentro de este grupo viral debido a la evidencia de transmisión interpersonal limitada. El objetivo de esta revisión narrativa es actualizar la evidencia disponible sobre la transmisión humano-humano del ANDV y analizar sus implicaciones clínicas y epidemiológicas. Se realizó una búsqueda bibliográfica narrativa en PubMed/MEDLINE y Google Scholar, incluyendo estudios epidemiológicos, revisiones y trabajos experimentales relevantes. Los brotes descritos en Argentina y Chile, junto con estudios moleculares y modelos animales, apoyan la existencia de transmisión interpersonal en contextos de contacto estrecho y prolongado, especialmente durante fases iniciales de la enfermedad. La detección de ARN viral en saliva y secreciones respiratorias aporta plausibilidad biológica a este fenómeno. La capacidad de transmisión interpersonal del ANDV posee implicaciones relevantes para el aislamiento, el rastreo de contactos y la vigilancia epidemiológica en áreas endémicas. Hantaviruses constitute a group of viruses responsible for emerging zoonotic diseases primarily transmitted by rodents. Andes virus (ANDV), endemic to South America, is unique among hantaviruses because of evidence supporting limited person-to-person transmission. The aim of this narrative review is to summarize current evidence regarding interpersonal transmission of ANDV and its clinical and epidemiological implications. A narrative literature search was conducted in PubMed/MEDLINE and Google Scholar including epidemiological studies, reviews, and experimental reports. Outbreaks described in Argentina and Chile, together with molecular studies and animal models, support the existence of person-to-person transmission in settings involving close and prolonged contact, particularly during the early stages of disease. Detection of viral RNA in saliva and respiratory secretions provides biological plausibility for this phenomenon. The transmissibility of ANDV has relevant implications for patient isolation, contact tracing, and epidemiological surveillance in endemic regions.

papers.title: Differential PCDH1 usage by Laguna Negra and Black Creek Canal hantaviruses
papers.abstract: Abstract Laguna Negra virus and Black Creek Canal virus are hantaviruses associated with hantavirus cardiopulmonary syndrome (HCPS), but their cellular entry receptors have not been defined. We used replication-competent recombinant vesicular stomatitis viruses (rVSVs) bearing hantavirus Gn/Gc glycoprotein complexes to compare entry by these viruses, the Old World rodent-borne Dabieshan virus and Tigray virus, and the shrew-borne Cao Bang virus and Amga virus. All six Gn/Gc complexes supported infection of primary human pulmonary microvascular endothelial cells, with virus-specific efficiencies and kinetics. Genetic ablation of protocadherin-1 (PCDH1) reduced infection mediated by Laguna Negra virus and Black Creek Canal virus Gn/Gc in human osteosarcoma and endothelial cells, whereas PCDH1 re-expression restored susceptibility. Both viruses were captured by a soluble PCDH1 protein comprising the first two extracellular cadherin domains. Infection was also inhibited by a soluble decoy containing the first cadherin domain, and by an antibody specific to that domain, indicating that the first PCDH1 cadherin domain mediates viral engagement. Black Creek Canal Gn/Gc-bearing rVSVs incorporated less Gn/Gc and showed lower apparent capture by PCDH1 than Laguna Negra virus and Andes virus Gn/Gc-bearing particles, even after normalization for glycoprotein abundance. In contrast, PCDH1 depletion did not detectably alter infection mediated by the other four hantavirus Gn/Gc complexes. Thus, Laguna Negra virus and Black Creek Canal virus use PCDH1 for efficient entry but differ in apparent receptor engagement and responses to PCDH1-directed inhibitors, whereas all six viruses are potently neutralized by the broadly reactive Gn/Gc-directed antibody ADI-42898. Importance The receptors used by many medically important hantaviruses remain incompletely characterized. Using BSL2-compatible rVSVs bearing hantavirus glycoproteins, we show that Laguna Negra virus and Black Creek Canal virus, two hantaviruses associated with human cardiopulmonary disease, used protocadherin-1 (PCDH1) for efficient entry into human cells. PCDH1-directed inhibitors blocked infection, but the two viruses differed in apparent receptor engagement and inhibitor sensitivity, showing that PCDH1 usage is not uniform even among closely related viruses. Gn/Gc complexes from four additional divergent hantaviruses carried by shrews and Old World rodents infected primary human endothelial cells without detectable PCDH1 dependence, emphasizing the need to identify alternative entry factors. A broadly reactive antibody neutralized every virus in the study panel, supporting conserved viral glycoprotein surfaces as therapeutic targets when receptor usage is diverse or unknown.

Mammalian hantaviruses (family Hantaviridae, order 62 Elliovirales) are emerging zoonotic pathogens that cause severe, often fatal illness in 63 humans after transmission from chronically infected small-mammal reservoirs, 64 manifesting as hemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome (HFRS) in Eurasia and 65 hantavirus cardiopulmonary syndrome (HCPS) in the Americas (2, 3). The public health 66 significance of hantaviruses is underscored by their recurring emergence, including a 67 multi-country HCPS outbreak in April-May 2026, which involved limited secondary 68 transmission and resulted in three reported deaths (4–6). Despite significant morbidity 69 and high case-fatality rates approaching 40% for HCPS, no FDA-approved 70 prophylactics or antiviral therapeutics are currently available (7). Cellular entry of 71 hantaviruses is orchestrated entirely by the envelope glycoprotein complex Gn/Gc (8, 72 9). Gn and Gc are synthesized as a single polyprotein precursor encoded by the 73 medium (M) genomic segment, co-translationally cleaved by cellular signal peptidases, 74 and assemble into spike-like tetramers of Gn/Gc heterodimers on the virion envelope 75 (8–11)These glycoproteins coordinate entry: the membrane-distal Gn subunit likely 76 mediates host receptor engagement, while the class II fusion protein Gc drives low-pH- 77 dependent membrane fusion within late endosomes envelope (8–12) Despite the 78 identification of dozens of hantavirus species across rodent and insectivore hosts 79 globally, host entry receptors and neutralization vulnerabilities for most divergent 80 species remain undefined (10, 13, 14). 81 Candidate hantavirus attachment factors and receptors initially identified through 82 antibody blockade, ligand competition, or in vitro binding assays include β1, β2, and β3 83 integrins, decay-accelerating factor (DAF/CD55), and gC1qR complement receptor (15– 84 19). However, CRISPR/Cas9-mediated loss-of-function screens in human 85 microvascular endothelial cells, a primary in vivo target cell type, demonstrated that 86 knockout of ITGB1, ITGB3, or DAF had little or no effect on infection by a panel of 87 virulent hantaviruses, indicating that these molecules are dispensable for endothelial 88 cell entry (20). Unbiased haploid-genetic screening instead identified protocadherin-1 89 (PCDH1) as an essential entry receptor for Andes virus (ANDV, Orthohantavirus 90 andesense) and Sin Nombre virus (SNV, Orthohantavirus sinnombreense): its 91 membrane-distal extracellular cadherin domain 1 (EC1) directly binds Gn/Gc, and 92 genetic ablation of PCDH1 in cultured cells and Syrian hamsters protects against ANDV 93 infection and lethal disease (21). Point mutations within the EC1 contact surface disrupt 94 infection, establishing PCDH1-EC1 as the functional interface (22). Although PCDH1 95 usage has been established for multiple hantaviruses, the glycoprotein determinants 96 that govern receptor recognition across divergent lineages remain incompletely defined 97 (20–22). PCDH1 usage has also been documented beyond the canonical New World 98 clade, including in vole- and mole-borne viruses (23), but its distribution across other 99 rodent- and shrew-borne clades has yet to be fully mapped. 100 Gn/Gc amino acid sequences differ by roughly 40-60% between hantavirus lineages, 101 and most glycoprotein-directed monoclonal antibodies (mAbs) raised or isolated against 102 one species show little heterologous neutralization (24, 25). Consequently, broadly 103 active entry inhibitors may need to target either conserved virus-receptor interfaces or 104 rare, functionally constrained epitopes on the viral spike (11, 21, 24, 25). On the host 105 side, the EC1-specific mAb-3305, soluble histidine-tagged PCDH1 ectodomain proteins 106 containing EC1-2 or EC1-4 (sEC1-2, sEC1-4), and a human Fc-tagged soluble EC1 107 decoy (EC1-Fc) block PCDH1-Gn/Gc engagement and neutralize PCDH1-dependent 108 viruses (21–23). Conversely, targeting conserved epitopes on the viral spike can 109 provide broad neutralization across clades. In particular, mAb-42898, isolated from a 110 Puumala virus (PUUV, Orthohantavirus puumalaense)-convalescent individual, binds a 111 quaternary epitope bridging the Gn capping loop and Gc fusion loops, neutralizes 112 multiple HCPS- and HFRS-causing viruses, and protects rodents against lethal 113 challenge (24, 26). Evaluating an expanded panel of uncharacterized Gn/Gc complexes 114 against both receptor-targeted and spike-targeted approaches can reveal conserved 115 viral vulnerabilities and inform the development of broadly active therapeutics. 116 Functional entry studies of less-characterized hantaviruses are constrained by the 117 limited availability of cultivable isolates and the requirement for biosafety level 3 or 4 118 (BSL3/4) containment for pathogenic hantaviruses (10). Here, we generated replication- 119 competent recombinant vesicular stomatitis viruses (rVSVs) expressing an enhanced 120 green fluorescent protein (eGFP) reporter and bearing codon-optimized Gn/Gc 121 complexes from six ecologically and phylogenetically distinct hantaviruses: the HCPS- 122 associated Black Creek Canal virus (BCCV, Orthohantavirus nigrorivense; carried by 123 Hispid cotton rat) (27) and Laguna Negra virus (LANV, Orthohantavirus mamorense; 124 small vesper mouse) (28); the Old World rodent-borne Dabieshan virus (DBSV, 125 Orthohantavirus dabieshanense; Chinese white-bellied rat) (29) and Tigray virus (TIGV, 126 Orthohantavirus tigrayense; Ethiopian white-footed mouse) (30, 31); the shrew-borne 127 Cao Bang virus (CBNV, Orthohantavirus caobangense; Chinese mole shrew) (32) and 128 Amga virus (MGAV, Orthohantavirus artybashense; Laxmann's shrew) (33, 34). This 129 panel includes viruses with distinct and incompletely defined zoonotic relevance. TIGV 130 circulates in peridomestic rodents in Ethiopia, where orthohantavirus-reactive antibodies 131 were detected in human sera (35). DBSV is genetically related to the prototypic HFRS- 132 causing Hantaan virus (HTNV), whereas CBNV and MGAV are shrew-borne viruses 133 with no established association with human disease (13, 29). 134 BCCV and LANV are particularly notable because authentic isolates exist for both, and 135 each has been studied extensively in epidemiologic, reservoir, and animal-model 136 settings. BCCV persists asymptomatically with horizontal transmission in its natural 137 reservoir but is uniformly lethal in immunosuppressed Syrian hamsters (36–38), 138 whereas LANV causes HCPS across South America and lethal pulmonary disease in 139 Turkish hamsters (39). Despite this substantial body of work, the receptor requirements 140 of both viruses remain undefined: BCCV entry was last examined before any hantavirus 141 receptor was identified (40) and neither virus has been tested for PCDH1 dependence. 142 To recover replication-competent rVSVs bearing Old World rodent-borne and shrew- 143 borne glycoproteins, we engineered Gn/Gc constructs using previously established 144 HTNV-based rescue-enhancing substitutions (23, 41). Here we show that all six Gn/Gc 145 complexes mediate infection of human microvascular endothelial cells, consistent with 146 systematic pseudotype screens showing that receptor-binding proteins from diverse 147 animal viruses can function broadly in human cells (1). CRISPR/Cas9-based genetic 148 depletion and cDNA complementation in human cells demonstrated that infection 149 mediated by glycoproteins of BCCV and LANV—but not those of DBSV, TIGV, CBNV, 150 or MGAV—depends on PCDH1. Concordantly, BCCV and LANV glycoproteins bound 151 soluble PCDH1 with different efficiencies in sEC1-2 capture ELISAs, were competitively 152 blocked at this interface by EC1-specific mAb-3305, and were neutralized by EC1-Fc 153 and mAb-3305 in endothelial cell infection assays. Finally, ADI-42898 bound all six 154 Gn/Gc-bearing particles and neutralized them with variable potency that correlated with 155 naturally occurring amino acid variation at epitope sites corresponding to PUUV 156 residues Q98, E750, and E768. Together, our findings expand the known diversity of 157 hantavirus receptor usage and define human endothelial cell susceptibility and antibody 158 sensitivity profiles across an expanded spectrum of hantavirus glycoproteins. 159 Results 160 Gn/Gc complexes from divergent rodent- and shrew-borne hantaviruses mediate 161 infection of human endothelial cells 162 We evaluated whether Gn/Gc glycoproteins from six phylogenetically and ecologically 163 distinct hantaviruses could mediate infection of human endothelial cells. The panel 164 included the New World rodent-borne viruses Black Creek Canal virus (BCCV) and 165 Laguna Negra virus (LANV), the Old World rodent-borne viruses Dabieshan virus 166 (DBSV) and Tigray virus (TIGV), and the shrew-borne Cao Bang virus (CBNV) and 167 Amga virus (MGAV) (Fig. 1A). Although cell culture isolates are available for BCCV and 168 LANV (27, 28), authenticated isolates have not been reported for DBSV, TIGV, CBNV 169 or MGAV, which are known from viral sequences recovered from reservoir tissues. 170 To examine Gn/Gc-mediated entry under BSL2 conditions, we generated replication- 171 competent recombinant vesicular stomatitis viruses (rVSVs) in which the native VSV G 172 open reading frame was replaced with the Gn/Gc open reading frame from LANV, 173 BCCV, DBSV, CBNV, TIGV, or MGAV. An enhanced green fluorescent protein (eGFP) 174 reporter was included in the first transcriptional unit to permit quantitation of infected 175 cells (Fig. 1B, top). Consistent with established rVSV rescue strategies for Old World 176 rodent-borne, mole-, and shrew-borne viruses, constructs from DBSV, CBNV, TIGV, 177 and MGAV contained the Hantaan virus (HTNV)-derived rescue-enhancing substitutions 178 I532K in the Gn cytoplasmic tail and S1094L in the membrane-proximal stem of Gc 179 ectodomain (23, 41) (Fig. 1B bottom). In selected constructs, adjacent residues were 180 also replaced with their HTNV counterparts. These modifications promote plasma- 181 membrane localization and rVSV incorporation of HTNV Gn/Gc and lie outside the 182 receptor-binding interface and the mapped neutralizing-antibody epitopes evaluated 183 here. 184 Recovery of rVSV-BCCV required an S430C substitution. Because cysteine is highly 185 conserved at the corresponding position among mammalian hantaviruses, the serine 186 reported in the deposited BCCV GenBank sequence may reflect a sequencing error 187 rather than authentic viral variation. Nanopore sequencing of rescued rVSV stocks 188 identified no additional nonsynonymous changes beyond the engineered substitutions, 189 except for G485R in rVSV-MGAV. This substitution has also been observed during 190 rescue of rVSV bearing the related Kenkeme virus Gn/Gc (23) but not for most other 191 hantavirus Gn/Gc proteins (20, 21, 42–44). G485, the terminal residue of the Gn 192 ectodomain, is highly conserved among hantaviruses; however, the functional 193 consequences of the G485R substitution remain unknown. 194 We then measured infection of primary human pulmonary microvascular endothelial 195 cells (HPMECs) over 48 h at a multiplicity of infection (MOI) of 1 (Fig. 1C and D). Virus 196 inputs were normalized using titers determined in permissive Huh-7.5.1 cells. At 12 h 197 postinfection (hpi), rVSV-LANV and rVSV-DBSV infection approached or exceeded that 198 of the rVSV-ANDV control, with approximately 30-40% of cells becoming eGFP positive 199 (Fig. 1C and D). Infection by these viruses and by rVSV-ANDV peaked between 24 and 200 36 hpi, reaching approximately 70-90% eGFP positive cells (Fig. 1D). In contrast, rVSV- 201 BCCV infection was only minimally detectable at 12 hpi, at approximately 4%, and 202 increased to a plateau of approximately 20% by 24 hpi (Fig. 1D). rVSV-CBNV, rVSV- 203 TIGV, and rVSV-MGAV produced slower and lower-level infection, becoming readily 204 detectable only at 48 hpi, when approximately 4-8% of cells were eGFP positive (Fig. 205 1C and D). 206 Thus, all six Gn/Gc complexes mediated infection of primary human endothelial cells 207 but differed substantially in infection efficiency and kinetics. These data establish human 208 endothelial-cell entry competence for LANV and BCCV Gn/Gc and provide functional 209 evidence that the Gn/Gc complexes of DBSV, TIGV, CBNV, and MGAV can mediate 210 cellular entry. 211 BCCV and LANV Gn/Gc-mediated infection depends on PCDH1 212 We next tested whether the Gn/Gc complexes in this panel require PCDH1 for entry. 213 Wild-type (WT), PCDH1-knockout cells transduced with empty vector (KO + EV), and 214 PCDH1-knockout cells complemented with PCDH1 cDNA (KO + PCDH1) were infected 215 with the indicated rVSVs. These genetic backgrounds in previously validated human 216 osteosarcoma U2OS and telomerase-immortalized human microvascular endothelial 217 (TIME) cell systems enable distinction between PCDH1-dependent and PCDH1- 218 independent hantavirus entry pathways (20–23). 219 In U2OS cells, PCDH1 ablation reduced infection by rVSV-BCCV and rVSV-LANV by 220 approximately 50-60%, similar to the reduction observed for the PCDH1-dependent 221 rVSV-ANDV control (Fig. 2A). PCDH1 re-expression restored rVSV-LANV and rVSV- 222 ANDV infection. Infection by rVSV-BCCV also increased after PCDH1 223 complementation, reaching levels above those observed in WT cells. In contrast, 224 PCDH1 status had little or no effect on infection by rVSV-DBSV, rVSV-CBNV, rVSV- 225 TIGV, and rVSV-MGAV, paralleling the well-established PCDH1-independent infection 226 of rVSV-HTNV. 227 We confirmed this phenotype in TIME cells, providing an endothelial cell context 228 relevant to hantavirus tropism. In these cells, PCDH1 knockout reduced rVSV-BCCV 229 and rVSV-LANV infection by approximately 75% relative to WT cells, comparable to the 230 reduction observed for rVSV-ANDV (Fig. 2B). rVSV-HTNV infection was not 231 significantly affected by PCDH1 knockout. analysis.background: Laguna Negra virus (LNV) and Black Creek Canal virus (BCCV) are hantaviruses that cause hantavirus cardiopulmonary syndrome (HCPS), but their cellular entry receptors have not been defined (A1).
analysis.methods: The study employed replication‑competent recombinant vesicular stomatitis viruses (rVSVs) bearing the Gn/Gc glycoprotein complexes of LNV, BCCV, and four other hantaviruses to assess entry into primary human pulmonary microvascular endothelial cells, using genetic ablation and re‑expression of protocadherin‑1 (PCDH1) and soluble PCDH1 reagents (A2).
analysis.results: Genetic ablation of PCDH1 reduced infection by LNV and BCCV Gn/Gc‑bearing rVSVs, which was restored by PCDH1 re‑expression; both viruses were captured by soluble PCDH1 ectodomain and blocked by a soluble EC1 decoy and an EC1‑specific antibody, indicating EC1 mediates engagement (A4,A6); BCCV particles incorporated less Gn/Gc and showed lower apparent capture than LNV (A7); PCDH1 loss did not affect entry of the other four hantavirus Gn/Gc complexes (A8); all six viruses were potently neutralized by the broadly reactive Gn/Gc‑directed antibody ADI‑42898 (A9).
analysis.contribution: The work identifies PCDH1 as an entry receptor for two HCPS‑associated hantaviruses and shows that PCDH1 usage varies even among closely related viruses, emphasizing the need to identify alternative entry factors (A11); it also demonstrates that a broadly reactive Gn/Gc antibody can neutralize diverse hantaviruses, supporting conserved glycoprotein surfaces as therapeutic targets (A14).
analysis.limitations: Limitations not reported in the supplied evidence.

analysis.summary_en: Background: LNV and BCCV cause HCPS but their entry receptors are unknown. Methods: rVSVs bearing Gn/Gc of LNV, BCCV and four other hantaviruses infected primary human pulmonary microvascular endothelial cells, with PCDH1 knocked out, re‑expressed, and blocked by soluble ectodomain and antibodies. Results: PCDH1 knockout reduced LNV and BCCV entry, restored by re‑expression; both viruses bound soluble PCDH1 and were inhibited by an EC1 decoy and EC1‑specific antibody, indicating EC1 mediates engagement; BCCV particles incorporated less Gn/Gc and showed lower capture than LNV, while the other four viruses entered independently of PCDH1; all six viruses were neutralized by the Gn/Gc‑directed antibody ADI‑42898. Contribution: Demonstrates PCDH1 as a receptor for two HCPS hantaviruses with virus‑specific engagement differences and shows a broadly neutralizing antibody can target diverse hantaviruses. Limitations: Limitations not reported in the supplied evidence.

papers.title: Vaccines for the prevention of hantavirus fevers: An overview of results and development prospects
papers.abstract: INTRODUCTION. Hantavirus fevers, known as hemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome (HFRS) in Eurasia and hantavirus pulmonary syndrome (HPS) in the Americas, are natural focal diseases with a wide range of clinical manifestations. The causative agents are members of the genus Orthohantavirus , whose natural reservoirs are rodents of various species. There is currently no etiotropic therapy for these diseases. Specific prophylaxis through vaccination is available only in the DPRK, the Republic of Korea, and the People's Republic of China. An important objective is to provide the Russian and European markets with a relevant vaccine for HFRS prevention. Such a vaccine should be developed based on both time-proven approaches and the experience of modern developments. AIM. Analysis of the use of existing hantavirus vaccines and the specific features of vaccines under development, as well as assessment of the prospects for creating vaccines for HFRS prevention in the Russian Federation. DISCUSSION. All commercially available vaccine preparations are inactivated whole-virion vaccines based on the Hantaan and Seoul viruses. The effectiveness of these preparations varies, but a significant reduction in the incidence rate in regions with mass vaccination and a low incidence of adverse events have been noted. Several inactivated whole-virion vaccines based on relevant orthohantavirus strains have been developed in Russia. Some of these developments have successfully completed preclinical studies. The spectrum of hantavirus vaccine preparations under development includes subunit vaccines, vaccines based on virus-like particles (VLPs) and viral vectors, DNA vaccines, and mRNA vaccines. The primary immunogens are the surface glycoproteins Gn and Gc of hantaviruses. The closest to implementation into clinical practice are the DNA vaccines based on the Puumala and Hantaan viruses, which have undergone clinical trials (phase I). CONCLUSIONS. No vaccine for the prevention of hantavirus infections developed using virus-like particles (VLPs), viral vectors, or nucleic acids (DNA or mRNA) has undergone a full cycle of clinical trials or been licensed worldwide. On the contrary, well-established traditional technologies for manufacturing inactivated vaccines and their time-proven effectiveness provide a basis for their real prospects of practical application in the Russian Federation and other European countries.

papers.full_text: Вакцины для профилактики хантавирусных лихорадок: обзор результатов и перспектив разработок https://doi.org/10.30895/2221-996X-2026-26-3-324-335 Резюме ВВЕДЕНИЕ. Хантавирусные лихорадки, регистрируемые как геморрагическая лихорадка с почечным синдромом (ГЛПС) на Евроазиатском и хантавирусный пульмональный синдром (ХПС) на Американском континентах, представляют собой природно-очаговые болезни с широким диапазоном клинических проявлений. Возбудители — представители рода Orthohantavirus, резервуаром которых в природе являются грызуны различных видов. Этиотропной терапии хантавирусных лихорадок в настоящее время не существует. Специфическая профилактика в форме вакцинации проводится только в КНДР, Республике Корее и КНР. Важной задачей является обеспечение российского и европейского рынка актуальной вакциной для профилактики ГЛПС. Противохантавирусная вакцина должна разрабатываться как с учетом подходов, доказавших временем свою эффективность, так и опыта современных разработок. ЦЕЛЬ. Анализ применения существующих хантавирусных и особенностей разрабатываемых вакцин, а также оценка перспектив создания вакцин для профилактики ГЛПС в Российской Федерации. ОБСУЖДЕНИЕ. Все коммерчески доступные вакцинные препараты являются инактивированными цельновирионными вакцинами на основе вирусов Хантаан и Сеул. Эффективность этих препаратов различается, но отмечается существенное снижение заболеваемости в регионах с массовой вакцинацией и низкая частота побочных явлений. В России разработаны несколько инактивированных цельновирионных вакцин на основе актуальных штаммов ортохантавирусов. Некоторые из разработок успешно прошли доклинические испытания. Спектр разрабатываемых хантавирусных вакцинных препаратов представлен субъединичными вакцинами, вакцинами на основе вирусоподобных частиц и вирусных векторов, ДНК- и мРНК-вакцин. В качестве основных иммуногенов используются поверхностные гликопротеины Gn и Gc хантавирусов. Наиболее близко к внедрению в медицинскую практику оказались ДНК-вакцины на основе вирусов Пуумала и Хантаан, прошедшие клинические исследования (фаза I). ЗАКЛЮЧЕНИЕ. Ни один вакцинный препарат для профилактики хантавирусных инфекций, разработанный на основе вирусоподобных частиц, вирусных векторов, нуклеиновых кислот, не прошел полного цикла клинических испытаний и не лицензирован в мире. Напротив, отлаженные традиционные технологии изготовления инактивированных вакцин и их доказанная временем эффективность обусловливают реальные перспективы их практического применения в России и других европейских странах.
