Хантавирусные лихорадки, регистрируемые как геморрагическая лихорадка с почечным синдромом (ГЛПС) на Евроазиатском и хантавирусный пульмональный синдром (ХПС) на Американском континентах, представляют собой природно-очаговые болезни с широким диапазоном клинических проявлений. Возбудители — представители рода Orthohantavirus, резервуаром которых в природе являются грызуны различных видов. Этиотропной терапии хантавирусных лихорадок в настоящее время не существует. Специфическая профилактика в форме вакцинации проводится только в КНДР, Республике Корее и КНР. Важной задачей является обеспечение российского и европейского рынка актуальной вакциной для профилактики ГЛПС. Противохантавирусная вакцина должна разрабатываться как с учетом подходов, доказавших временем свою эффективность, так и опыта современных разработок. ЦЕЛЬ. Анализ применения существующих хантавирусных и особенностей разрабатываемых вакцин, а также оценка перспектив создания вакцин для профилактики ГЛПС в Российской Федерации. ОБСУЖДЕНИЕ. Все коммерчески доступные вакцинные препараты являются инактивированными цельновирионными вакцинами на основе вирусов Хантаан и Сеул. Эффективность этих препаратов различается, но отмечается существенное снижение заболеваемости в регионах с массовой вакцинацией и низкая частота побочных явлений. В России разработаны несколько инактивированных цельновирионных вакцин на основе актуальных штаммов ортохантавирусов. Некоторые из разработок успешно прошли доклинические испытания. Спектр разрабатываемых хантавирусных вакцинных препаратов представлен субъединичными вакцинами, вакцинами на основе вирусоподобных частиц и вирусных векторов, ДНК- и мРНК-вакцин. В качестве основных иммуногенов используются поверхностные гликопротеины Gn и Gc хантавирусов. Наиболее близко к внедрению в медицинскую практику оказались ДНК-вакцины на основе вирусов Пуумала и Хантаан, прошедшие клинические исследования (фаза I). ЗАКЛЮЧЕНИЕ. Ни один вакцинный препарат для профилактики хантавирусных инфекций, разработанный на основе вирусоподобных частиц, вирусных векторов, нуклеиновых кислот, не прошел полного цикла клинических испытаний и не лицензирован в мире. Напротив, отлаженные традиционные технологии изготовления инактивированных вакцин и их доказанная временем эффективность обусловливают реальные перспективы их практического применения в России и других европейских странах. analysis.background: Hantavirus fevers are natural focal diseases with a wide range of clinical manifestations and no etiotropic therapy (A1, F2, F3, F4). Prophylaxis by vaccination is currently limited to DPRK, Korea, and China (F5). The study aims to provide a vaccine for Russian and European markets (A5).

DNA vaccines for Puumala and Hantaan have reached phase I trials (A14, F15).
analysis.results: Effectiveness of inactivated vaccines varies but shows significant incidence reduction in mass‑vaccinated regions and low adverse events (A9, F10). Some Russian inactivated vaccines have completed preclinical studies (A10, A11). DNA vaccines have phase I data (A14).
analysis.contribution: Traditional inactivated vaccine technologies have proven effectiveness and realistic prospects for application in Russia and other European countries (A16). DNA vaccines are the closest to clinical implementation (A15).
analysis.limitations: No full‑cycle clinical trials or licensing exist for VLP, viral vector, or nucleic‑acid vaccines (A15, A16). Detailed efficacy data are not reported in the supplied evidence (not reported in the supplied evidence).

Contribution: Traditional inactivated vaccines have proven effectiveness and realistic prospects for use in Russia and Europe; DNA vaccines are closest to clinical implementation. Limitations: No full‑cycle trials or licensing for VLP, viral vector, or nucleic‑acid vaccines; detailed efficacy data are not reported.

papers.title: Network-Guided Drug Repurposing for Hantaan Virus Infection in Endothelial Cells: Pathway Analysis, Target Identification, and Mechanistic ODE Simulations
papers.abstract: Hantaviruses cause haemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome and hantavirus cardiopulmonary syndrome, which are together the cause of more than 200,000 human cases every year. However, no specific antiviral therapy is approved. Here, we develop a three-stage computational framework for systematic drug repurposing. Transcriptome-wide analysis of hantavirus-infected human endothelial cells showed a response dominated by interferon pathways. A STRING protein–protein interaction network and a composite network centrality score identified 15 hub genes, including ISG15, IRF1, CXCL10, STAT1, and DDX58. Druggability and literature analysis of these hubs provided 12 repurposing candidates across four priority tiers. An ordinary differential equation (ODE) model of type I interferon signalling then evaluated eight drug perturbations. Early IFN-β achieved the fastest viral clearance (3.5 days) with reduced CXCL10 output. Early JAK inhibition delayed clearance (4.9 days) and increased IRF1-driven CXCL10. Our simulation showed that IFN-β combined with an anti-CXCL10 monoclonal antibody produced the best balance between antiviral effect and CXCL10 output. A structural sensitivity analysis showed the antiviral predictions to hold under an alternative network topology, while the chemokine predictions depended on it. This computational pipeline prioritises candidate therapies and phase-specific combinations for preclinical hantavirus studies.

papers.title_zh: 基于网络的药物再利用用于 汉滩病毒 感染的内皮细胞:通路分析、靶点识别与机制性 ODE 模拟

analysis_zh.background: 汉坦病毒 引起肾综合征出血热,汉坦病毒心肺综合征 亦如此,两者合计每年导致超过 200,000 例人类感染,且尚未获批特异性抗病毒疗法。
analysis_zh.methods: 作者开发了一个三阶段计算框架:对汉坦病毒感染的人类内皮细胞进行全转录组分析,利用STRING蛋白-蛋白相互作用网络的中心性识别出15个枢纽基因,进行可药性和文献筛选得到12个再利用候选药物,并构建I型干扰素信号通路的常微分方程模型,以评估八种药物扰动的效果。
analysis_zh.results: 模拟显示,早期IFN-β实现最快的病毒清除(3.5天)并降低CXCL10水平;早期JAK抑制延迟清除(4.9天)且增加CXCL10;IFN-β联合抗CXCL10抗体能够获得最佳的抗病毒‐趋化因子平衡;敏感性分析表明,抗病毒预测对网络拓扑稳健,而趋化因子预测则依赖于拓扑结构。

papers.title: Climate change as an amplifier of hantavirus risk in South Asia: a neglected nexus.
papers.abstract: Hantavirus is seroepidemiologically established in South Asian human populations and rodent reservoirs, with anti-hantavirus antibodies confirmed in occupational risk groups in India, an independent association with chronic kidney disease demonstrated in Sri Lanka, and co-infection with leptospirosis identified in more than one-fifth of hospitalized leptospirosis patients. Despite this, the intersection of these findings with the region's intensifying monsoon floods, rapid urbanization, and climate-driven rodent ecology remains entirely unexamined. This letter highlights the neglected climate-hantavirus nexus, identifies structural vulnerabilities that amplify transmission risk in South Asia, and calls for integrated flood-response surveillance and One Health coordination across the region.
papers.journal: Transactions of the Royal Society of Tropical Medicine and Hygiene

papers.title: A noetic fractal-fractional dynamical formalism for history-dependent Seoul virus–Streptococcus pyogenes dual-pathogen interaction with physics-informed learning

source_records.title: A noetic fractal-fractional dynamical formalism for history-dependent Seoul virus–Streptococcus pyogenes dual-pathogen interaction with physics-informed learning

papers.full_text: A noetic fractal-fractional dynamical formalism for history-dependent Seoul virus–Streptococcus pyogenes dual-pathogen interaction with physics-informed learning Abstract Seoul virus is an important rodent-borne hantavirus that can cause serious illness in humans, while Streptococcus pyogenes is a clinically significant bacterial pathogen associated with a wide range of infections and severe complications. The interaction between these two infections is not well understood from a mathematical modeling perspective. In this work, we develop a fractal–fractional model to investigate the transmission and co-infection dynamics of Seoul virus and Streptococcus pyogenes. The model is described using the Atangana–Baleanu–Caputo fractal–fractional derivative so that the effects of memory and the nonuniform nature of disease transmission can be represented more realistically than in conventional integer-order models. Several mathematical properties of the proposed system are studied, including the existence and uniqueness of solutions and the behavior of the disease-free equilibrium. The basic reproduction number is obtained to identify the threshold conditions associated with the spread of the infections, and the Ulam–Hyers stability of the model is also examined. In addition to the theoretical analysis, a physics-informed neural network is constructed to approximate the solutions of the fractal–fractional system. The governing equations and initial conditions are incorporated into the neural-network training process, allowing the model structure to guide the numerical approximation. The simulations illustrate the influence of the fractional and fractal parameters on the evolution of the co-infection system and show that the PINN approach can reproduce the model dynamics with good accuracy. The findings suggest that combining fractal–fractional operators with physics-informed learning offers a useful way to study co-infectious disease systems in which memory, heterogeneity, and nonlinear interactions play an important role. papers.title_zh: 一种面向历史依赖的首尔病毒–化脓性链球菌双病原体相互作用的认知分形-分数动力学形式及物理信息学习

analysis_zh.background: 首尔病毒是一种啮齿动物传播的汉坦病毒,可导致严重的人类疾病,Streptococcus pyogenes是临床重要的细菌病原体;从数学建模角度看,它们的共感染动力学了解甚少(F1, F2)。
analysis_zh.methods: 作者采用Atangana–Baleanu–Caputo分形-分数导数构建双病原体模型,以捕捉记忆效应和异质性,分析解的存在性、唯一性、无疾病平衡以及基本再生数,评估Ulam–Hyers稳定性,并构建物理信息神经网络(PINN),将控制方程和初始条件纳入用于数值近似(F3‐F8)。
analysis_zh.results: 模拟表明,分数和分形参数影响共感染动力学,且PINN能够以较高精度再现模型行为(F9, F10)。

papers.title: Hantavirus in Dentistry: Occupational Exposure Considerations and a Proposed Tiered Infection Prevention and Control Framework-A Narrative Review.
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Objective The aim of this study is to synthesize evidence on hantavirus transmission and occupational exposure pathways relevant to dentistry, and to propose an evidence‐informed tiered infection prevention and control (IPC) framework that distinguishes established from theoretical risk. Material and Methods The initial narrative search covered database inception through May 15, 2026 in MEDLINE/PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, Scopus, Google Scholar, and WHO/CDC/ECDC/OSHA sources, followed by a targeted PubMed/MEDLINE and public‐health guidance update through August 18, 2026. Approximately 1450 records were identified. After duplicate removal, 1070 records were subjected to title/abstract screening, 215 full‐text records were assessed for eligibility, and 45 sources were included in the final synthesis, comprising 34 peer‐reviewed publications and 11 gray‐literature or public‐health guidance sources. Results Environmental exposure to infected‐rodent contamination is the established occupational pathway. Limited person‐to‐person transmission is documented for the Andes virus (ANDV), but no dental transmission has been reported. ANDV RNA and culture‐based infectivity have been demonstrated in some oral/respiratory fluids; however, dental‐aerosol transmission has not been shown. Dental‐specific occupational risk therefore remains unquantified. Conclusions No dental transmission has been documented, and patient‐related risk remains uncertain. Standard precautions and rodent control are foundational; suspected or confirmed ANDV warrants transmission‐based precautions and airborne precautions for aerosol‐generating procedures according to current guidance. The proposed dental tiers are evidence‐informed, author‐derived, and unvalidated.

analysis.background: The review was undertaken to synthesize evidence on hantavirus transmission and occupational exposure pathways relevant to dentistry and to propose a tiered infection‑prevention framework (A1).
analysis.main_directions: It highlights environmental exposure to rodent‑contaminated material as the established occupational route (A5) and notes limited person‑to‑person transmission of Andes virus, though no dental transmission has been reported (A6).
analysis.current_state: Environmental exposure is the confirmed risk, Andes virus can be transmitted between people in rare cases, and no documented dental transmission exists, leaving patient‑related risk uncertain (A5, A6, A10).
analysis.gaps: The magnitude of dental‑specific occupational risk remains unquantified and the proposed tiered IPC framework is author‑derived and unvalidated (A9, A13).
analysis.future_research: Empirical studies to quantify dental exposure risk and validation of the tiered IPC framework are needed (A9, A13).

analysis.summary_en: Background: The review synthesizes hantavirus transmission evidence for dentistry and proposes a tiered IPC framework (A1). Main directions: It focuses on rodent‑environmental exposure as the established risk and limited Andes virus person‑to‑person spread, with no dental cases reported (A5, A6). Current state: Environmental exposure is confirmed, Andes virus can transmit rarely, and dental transmission is undocumented, making patient risk uncertain (A5, A6, A10). Gaps: Dental‑specific risk is unquantified and the tiered framework lacks validation (A9, A13). Future research: Studies to measure dental exposure risk and to validate the IPC tiers are required (A9, A13).

papers.title_zh: 汉坦病毒 在牙科:职业暴露考虑及提出的分层感染预防与控制框架——叙述性综述。

analysis_zh.background: 本综述旨在综合关于 汉坦病毒 传播及与牙科相关的职业暴露途径的证据,并提出分层感染预防框架 (A1)。
analysis_zh.main_directions: 它强调对鼠类污染材料的环境暴露是已确立的职业途径 (A5),并指出 安第斯病毒 的人际传播有限,尽管尚未报告牙科传播案例 (A6)。
analysis_zh.current_state: 环境暴露是已确认的风险,安第斯病毒 在极少数情况下可在人与人之间传播,且未有牙科传播的记录,导致与患者相关的风险仍不确定 (A5, A6, A10)。
analysis_zh.gaps: 牙科特定职业风险的规模尚未量化,且提出的分层 IPC 框架为作者自行制定,未经过验证 (A9, A13)。
analysis_zh.future_research: 需要开展实证研究以量化牙科暴露风险,并验证分层 IPC 框架 (A9, A13)。

papers.title: Open ecological, genomic and digital behavioural data resolve the 2026 MV Hondius Andes virus outbreak to the southern-Andean reservoir zone
papers.abstract: The 2026 Andes virus (ANDV) outbreak aboard the MV Hondius cruise ship resulted in 11 confirmed cases and 3 deaths and raised questions regarding the origin of infection, with much media focus resting on a landfill in Tierra del Fuego. We evaluated competing exposure hypotheses by assembling open data on reservoir host occurrences, rodent serosurveys, and historical ANDV outbreaks along with the index case’s self-documented, publicly-posted citizen-science digital record of their movements. Historical outbreaks associated with human-to-human transmission were concentrated within a restricted region spanning southern Chile and adjacent western Argentina, coinciding with the distribution of the principal reservoir host, Oligoryzomys longicaudatus , and areas identified as elevated risk by multiple ecological and genetic models. The index case was documented within this transmission focus shortly before the putative exposure period. Together, our open data approach was able to rapidly locate initial exposure within the established ANDV transmission focus and develop scenarios to prioritise further epidemiological investigation.

papers.title: [Nucleoside analogues in etiotropic therapy of hantavirus fevers].
papers.abstract: Hantavirus fevers (HF) are caused by pathogenic orthohantaviruses and are classified into two clinical forms: hemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome (HFRS), reported in Eurasia, and hantavirus pulmonary syndrome (HPS), reported in the Americas. HF are characterised by an acute course with predominant involvement of internal organs: HFRS is mainly associated with kidney damage, while HPS is characterised by severe lung injury. Both diseases may also affect the central nervous and endocrine systems. In addition, hantavirus fevers are marked by severe complications during the acute phase and a prolonged recovery period. Currently, there is neither a WHO-approved vaccine nor any effective etiotropic anti-hantavirus therapy. The development of antiviral treatment strategies focuses on preventing orthohantavirus entry into cells or suppressing their intracellular replication. One of the main directions in the search for effective anti-hantavirus therapy is the low-molecular-weight compounds development and testing, many of which have demonstrated pronounced antiviral activity against orthohantaviruses through direct or indirect effects on viral RNA polymerase function. The review shows that new antiviral nucleoside compounds development and study has promising potential, as well as their combined use for effective etiotropic, pathogenetic and symptomatic treatment of hantavirus fevers.

analysis.background: Hantavirus fevers (HF) are caused by pathogenic orthohantaviruses and present as HFRS in Eurasia and HPS in the Americas.
analysis.main_directions: Antiviral strategies target viral entry or replication, with emphasis on low‑molecular‑weight compounds that inhibit the viral RNA polymerase.
analysis.current_state: No WHO‑approved vaccine or effective etiotropic therapy exists for HF.
analysis.gaps: HF cause severe acute complications and prolonged recovery, highlighting unmet therapeutic needs.
analysis.future_research: Further development and clinical testing of novel nucleoside analogues, alone or combined with pathogenetic and symptomatic agents, is recommended.

analysis.summary_en: Background: Hantavirus fevers are caused by orthohantaviruses and appear as HFRS in Eurasia and HPS in the Americas. Main directions: Antiviral work focuses on blocking entry or replication, especially low‑molecular‑weight inhibitors of the viral RNA polymerase. Current state: No WHO‑approved vaccine or effective etiotropic treatment exists. Gaps: Severe acute complications and long recovery periods remain unmet. Future research: Advance and test new nucleoside analogues, alone or in combination with pathogenetic and symptomatic therapies.

papers.title: [Andes virus aboard the MV Hondius: Transnational public health challenges in ocean-going cruise travel].
papers.abstract: This article analyzes the cluster of Andes virus infections that occurred aboard the expedition vessel MV Hondius during a transatlantic crossing. Drawing on publicly available information released by the World Health Organization, the European Centre for Disease Prevention and Control, and the US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention, it examines the key characteristics of this event: probable exposure in a natural reservoir area in South America before embarkation, limited human-to-human transmission in a closed maritime environment, difficulties in early case recognition, and the complexity of international contact tracing. The analysis shows that the vessel itself was not the source of the virus, but rather a setting in which public health risks were amplified due to prolonged cohabitation, limited onboard medical resources, and the cross-border mobility of passengers. Finally, the article highlights the importance of stratified contact management, timely reporting, effective international cooperation, and clear risk communication to avoid both underestimation of the risk and unnecessary public panic.

source_records.abstract: This article analyzes the cluster of Andes virus infections that occurred aboard the expedition vessel MV Hondius during a transatlantic crossing. Drawing on publicly available information released by the World Health Organization, the European Centre for Disease Prevention and Control, and the US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention, it examines the key characteristics of this event: probable exposure in a natural reservoir area in South America before embarkation, limited human-to-human transmission in a closed maritime environment, difficulties in early case recognition, and the complexity of international contact tracing. The analysis shows that the vessel itself was not the source of the virus, but rather a setting in which public health risks were amplified due to prolonged cohabitation, limited onboard medical resources, and the cross-border mobility of passengers. Finally, the article highlights the importance of stratified contact management, timely reporting, effective international cooperation, and clear risk communication to avoid both underestimation of the risk and unnecessary public panic.
